reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need the order list so I can see which customers are in this batch. I'll check the orders first, then confirm the refunds against the ledger.
Next I need the refunds list so I can check W2's reported refunds against the ledger before paying anyone.
The refunds list matches W2's report exactly, so the ledger agrees with the handoff. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 54385 matches my own check: orders 39447 + 33625 = 73072, less the 18687 refund on order 203, gives 54385. Next I'll get birch's balance.
Birch's net of 29147 matches my own check: orders 4135 + 39885 = 44020, less refunds 3873 + 11000 = 14873. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I'll fetch its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 33079 matches my check: orders 30107 + 2972 = 33079, with no refunds on cobalt's orders. All three balances agree with the ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme for 54385.
Acme's payout of 54385 is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance is 29147, so I'll record that payout.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's verified net balance is 33079. That's the last customer in the batch, so I'll record its payout now.
All three customers have been paid their verified net balances, and each record_payout returned ok. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the payout report.
